name: Samsung Galaxy S9
summary: ztOS's first phone, and the reference port. Mainline Linux 7.1 with the Exynos 9810 drivers, booting from the phone's internal storage, with TWRP left in RECOVERY. Runs ztOS daily.
photo_caption: ztOS's Start screen on the Galaxy S9
specs: 4× Mongoose M3 at 2.7 GHz, 4× Cortex-A55 at 1.8 GHz
Mainline Linux 7.1, modules for the phone's hardware

install.warning: This erases the phone. Android and everything in its storage are replaced. The phone's IMEI and modem calibration (the EFS partitions) are never touched, and the stock Android partitions stay, because the modem needs them.
requirements: A Linux computer (x86-64 or ARM) with about 15 GB free and an internet connection
The bootloader unlocked (Settings > Developer options > OEM unlocking in Android) and TWRP for starlte flashed to RECOVERY with Odin or Heimdall
A USB cable, and the phone charged above 50%
On Arch Linux, the build tools: `sudo pacman -S --needed util-linux libarchive dosfstools mtools e2fsprogs qemu-user-static qemu-user-static-binfmt android-tools`

steps.title: Back up the phone
steps.text: Everything in Android's storage is erased.

steps.title: Start TWRP and connect the phone
steps.text: Turn the phone off, then hold Volume Up, Bixby and Power until TWRP appears. Plug it into the computer: `adb devices` shows it as `recovery`.

steps.title: Get ztOS on the computer
steps.text: `git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Zerone-Laboratories/ztOS.git`, then `cd ztOS` (in a clone you already have, `git submodule update --init` fetches the S9's kernel tree). `installer/ztos doctor` says whether the computer is ready.

steps.title: Build and install
steps.text: `installer/ztos install --target starlte --mode build-install`. It asks for a user name, password, the phone's name and your time zone, then builds the system and the boot image (30 to 60 minutes; the build never needs sudo).

steps.title: Confirm the writes
steps.text: Answer yes to write the boot image to BOOT (it is read back to check it), then type `ERASE` to write the system to USERDATA. It is written in checked 256 MiB pieces: if the cable comes out, run the same command again and it carries on.

steps.title: Restart into ztOS
steps.text: Let the installer restart the phone, or hold Power, Volume Up and Volume Down. The first start takes about a minute while the system grows to fill the storage, then the Welcome app shows how ztOS is used. Android apps are set up in the background on the first start (Waydroid downloads its images once).

install.after: If the phone ever fails to start, it goes back to TWRP by itself: start again from step 2. Once a BETA-1 release is published, `--mode download` installs the prebuilt image instead of building it (user `zerone`, password `toor`; change it at once).

notes.title: The modem or sensor hub doesn't come up
notes.text: It tends to follow a forced reboot or a crash. One pass through TWRP brings them back: `systemctl reboot --reboot-argument=recovery`, then `adb shell reboot` once TWRP is up. A full power-off also works.

notes.title: A driver that crashed while loading is skipped at the next boot
notes.text: So a crash can't become a boot loop. Remove its mark file under `/var/lib` to try it again.

notes.title: Reboot rather than unload a driver
notes.text: A failed module unload has left the phone unable to shut down.

notes.title: Keep the stock Android partitions
notes.text: The installer writes only BOOT and USERDATA; the modem needs the rest.

notes.title: Getting back in
notes.text: If Arch doesn't come up, the initramfs opens a rescue shell on the USB network. If the kernel hangs, a watchdog resets the phone into TWRP after 30 seconds. Download mode, which can't be overwritten, can always put the stock firmware back.
